name: Increment/Decrement Operators (Case 3)
description: Construct a program that performs increment/decrement operations on variable a (with initial value of 6) and variable b (with initial value of 1) and prints the following output as the result of these operations:\n5\n7

comments.content: We define variable a and set its initial value to 6.
We define variable b and set its initial value to 1.
The expression in this println statement produces the first output. The addition operator uses the decremented value of variable b (i.e., 0), thus generating the result of 5.

--b evaluates to 0 because variable b holds 1 and it gets decremented by 1 before the right-hand side of the addition operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the addition operator will be 0.
Note that when we have pre-decrement operator, the variable gets decremented by 1 and the updated value of that variable will be used in the statement.
The expression in this println statement produces the second output. The addition operator uses the original value of variable a before it gets decremented but incremented value of variable b.

a-- evaluates to 6 and then decrements variable a by 1. Therefore, the value on the left-hand side of the addition operator will be 6.
++b evaluates to 1 because, when program reaches here, variable b holds 0 and it gets incremented by 1 before the right-hand side of the addition operator is evaluated. Therefore, the value on the right-hand side of the addition operator will be 1.

Note that when we have post-decrement operator, the variable gets decremented by 1, but the original value of that variable will be used in the statement. Also note that when we have pre-increment operator, the variable gets incremented by 1 and the updated value of that variable will be used in the statement.
